props.gloss_en: R' Yosei (the mishna): this is [one] of the leniencies of Beit Shammai and the stringencies of Beit Hillel
the attempted answer: eating itself is between them -- the first tanna has them dispute only placing, and R' Yosei says eating itself is a leniency of Beit Shammai

the baraita: R' Yosei says six things are leniencies of Beit Shammai and stringencies of Beit Hillel, and this is one: fowl goes up with cheese on the table and is not eaten -- Beit Shammai; Beit Hillel: it neither goes up nor is eaten
rather, this is what it teaches: who is the first tanna? R' Yosei
whoever says a thing in the name of the one who said it brings redemption to the world, as it is said 'and Esther told the king in the name of Mordecai' (Est 2:22)
Agra: fowl and cheese are eaten be'apikoren
he taught it and he said it: without washing the hands
and without wiping the mouth
they brought him cheese -- he ate; they brought him meat -- he ate, and did not wash his hands
Rav Yitzchak: that applies at night; but by day -- I see
the baraita: Beit Shammai say: one wipes [the mouth]
and Beit Hillel say: one rinses
reading 1: Beit Shammai -- wipe, no need to rinse; Beit Hillel -- rinse, no need to wipe
reading 2: Beit Shammai -- wipe, no need to rinse; Beit Hillel -- rinse as well
reading 3: Beit Shammai -- wipe, and the same for rinsing; Beit Hillel -- rinse, and the same for wiping; each said one thing and they do not disagree
R' Zeira: wiping the mouth is only with bread
and that is with wheat [bread]; with barley -- not
and wheat too we said only cold; but hot -- it sticks
and that is with soft [bread]; with hard -- not
and the halakha: everything serves as wiping, except flour, dates and vegetables
the first understanding: Rav Asi asked how long between meat and cheese, and R' Yochanan answered: not at all
Rav Chisda: one who ate meat is forbidden to eat cheese
[one who ate] cheese is permitted to eat meat
rather: [Rav Asi asked] how long between cheese and meat? [R' Yochanan] said to him: not at all
meat between the teeth -- what is it? [Rav Chisda] read over him: 'the meat was yet between their teeth' (Num 11:33)
Father, eating meat at this hour, would not eat cheese until this hour tomorrow
Mar Ukva: in this I am vinegar son of wine compared to Father -- at this meal I do not eat [cheese], at another meal I eat
Father would inspect his property twice a day
Shmuel: in this I am vinegar son of wine compared to Father -- I inspect only once
Shmuel: one who inspects his property every day finds an istera
Abaye would inspect his property every single day
[to his sharecropper carrying wood] 'where are these going?' -- 'to the master's house' -- Abaye: 'the Rabbis already preceded you'
Rav Asi would inspect his property every day
